name: Furusund
description: Furusund is a short coastal-history loop in the northern Stockholm archipelago, mixing village lanes, sea views, maritime history, literary associations and exterior cultural landmarks. The current official PDF/Outdooractive route geometry supports about 6.9 km / 2 hours even though the public SAT page still says 7.2 km. The route is not SAT-marked; much follows local red markings, and it is best walked clockwise with the SAT map or GPX available.
utilities: Food and service are concentrated around Hotell Furusund / Furusunds Värdshus and Furusunds Hamn / Hamnkrog.
Furusunds Gästhamn has guest-harbor water, WC, shower and waste services, but these should be treated as seasonal/harbor-service facilities rather than guaranteed free public hiker infrastructure.

No grocery/resupply shop was confirmed with high confidence; Skärgårdsmacken/Furusundsmacken is a weak local fuel/post/kiosk/service candidate and should not be exposed as dependable grocery resupply.
No official campsite was found; lodging options include Hotell Furusund/Furusunds Värdshus and Villa Dagmar.

Furusundsbadplats and Myrudden are supported as simple local bathing/firepit spots by community/map/photo evidence. Do not label them municipal, monitored or water-quality tested beaches, and do not assume maintenance, firewood, toilets or water.
waterSources: Carry water unless guest-harbor water access has been verified for the date.
The best candidate refill is Furusunds Gästhamn, but it is harbor infrastructure and should be treated as seasonal/fee/service-dependent.
Hotell Furusund and Hamnkrogen may have customer toilets when open; do not treat them as public toilets.

Do not expose Duvkällan or road-ferry terminal facilities as water/toilet resources; iteration 2 found evidence the Duvkällan pump is broken/non-potable and no current reliable ferry-terminal toilet replacement.
notes: Route shape: short Furusund loop / round trip that can start at the ferry terminal or Furusunds Värdshus, recommended clockwise, following local red markings rather than SAT signs.
The route is not SAT-marked; much of it follows local red markings, but users should keep the SAT map/GPX available, especially through village/residential sections and intersections.
Recent 2026 AllTrails reports were generally positive and no active Furusund-specific SAT closure/reroute notice was found on April 26, 2026.
Check SAT news/report pages before hiking, but do not show a stored Furusund closure unless a current official notice appears.
The loop is short and village/coastal in character, but SAT labels it Moderate and notes a short steeper/rooty section on the west coast north of the bridge; it is not fully pram/wheelchair-friendly.
Expect a more village/residential feel than remote trail; one 2025 user report described substantial residential/concrete/manufactured path.

In winter/early spring, expect possible slippery, muddy or icy patches and reduced services. Furusund remains year-round reachable by bus/car, but users should verify return buses and ferry/boat connections for the travel date.

For Yxlan continuation, the free Trafikverket road ferry Furusund-Yxlan is normally the key link. A June 2025 ferry-capacity disruption was found, but no current April 2026 Furusundsleden disruption surfaced; traffic should be checked dynamically.
The route passes historic/literary houses; keep wording respectful and do not encourage close approach to private residences.
Do not reuse old Furusund tourist-info notes about 2019-2020 brygga repairs as current closure information.
Nearby Länsstyrelsen Furusundsfjärden nature reserve is not the main walking loop; do not apply its reserve-specific rules to the SAT route unless the user detours there.
